object.title: Stefán's circular-flow infimum conjecture for odd-regular class 2 graphs
object.statement:
Let $t$ be a positive integer, and let $Phi^{(2)}(2t+1)$ denote the infimum of $phi_c(G)$ over all $(2t+1)$-regular class $2$ graphs $G$, where $phi_c(G)$ is the circular flow number.

**Stefán's circular-flow infimum conjecture.**

$$
\Phi^{(2)}(2t+1)=2+\frac{2}{2t-1}.
$$

The source explicitly states that this conjecture is proved in the paper, so the claim is resolved.
object.source_name: Davide Mattiolo and Eckhard Steffen, “Edge colorings and circular flows on regular graphs”, arXiv:2001.02484 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.02484

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of January 2020); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

object.title: Stefán's circular-flow bound conjecture for class 1 odd-regular graphs
object.statement:
Let $t$ be a positive integer and let $G$ be a $(2t+1)$-regular class $1$ graph. Its circular flow number is denoted by $phi_c(G)$.

**Stefán's class 1 circular-flow bound conjecture.**

$$
\phi_c(G)\le 2+\frac{2}{t}.
$$

The source presents this as a conjecture and, in the supplied text, does not state that it has been proved or disproved.
object.source_name: Davide Mattiolo and Eckhard Steffen, “Edge colorings and circular flows on regular graphs”, arXiv:2001.02484 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.02484

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2020).

object.title: Las Vergnas's simplicial vertex conjecture for oriented matroids
object.statement: Let $G$ be the tope graph of an oriented matroid (OM), and let $r(G)$ be its rank. A vertex $v$ is **simplicial** if $\deg(v)=r(G)$. **Las Vergnas's conjecture.** Every OM has a simplicial vertex. This is known for realizable oriented matroids, for rank at most $3$, and for several additional classes, but remains open in general.
object.source_name: Kolja Knauer and Tilen Marc, “Corners and simpliciality in oriented matroids and partial cubes”, arXiv:2002.11403 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.11403

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2020). “Note that there is a hierarchical structure of these three open questions.”

object.title: Mandel's conjecture that every oriented matroid is Mandel
object.statement: An oriented matroid (OM) is **Mandel** if it has an expansion in general position such that the two associated antipodal oriented matroids are Euclidean. **Mandel's conjecture.** Every OM is Mandel. Since every Mandel OM has a simplicial vertex, this would imply Las Vergnas's simplicial vertex conjecture. The source describes it as a wishful-thinking statement and does not report a resolution.
object.source_name: Kolja Knauer and Tilen Marc, “Corners and simpliciality in oriented matroids and partial cubes”, arXiv:2002.11403 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.11403

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2020). “Note that there is a hierarchical structure of these three open questions.”

object.title: Murty's Sylvester–Gallai conjecture for oriented matroids
object.statement: Let $G$ be the tope graph of an oriented matroid of rank $r$. **Murty's conjecture.** $G$ contains a convex subgraph that is the Cartesian product of an edge and an antipodal graph of rank $r-2$. The conjecture generalizes the Sylvester–Gallai theorem. It is known for realizable and Mandel oriented matroids, but remains open in general.
object.source_name: Kolja Knauer and Tilen Marc, “Corners and simpliciality in oriented matroids and partial cubes”, arXiv:2002.11403 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.11403

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2020). “Note that there is a hierarchical structure of these three open questions.”

object.title: Subgroup closure conjecture for BCI-groups
object.statement: Let $G$ be a finite **BCI-group**, meaning that every bi-Cayley graph over $G$ is a BCI-graph, and let $H\leq G$ be a subgroup. **Subgroup closure conjecture.** Then $H$ is a BCI-group. This mirrors the known subgroup-closure property for CI-groups, but the supplied text gives no resolution status for the BCI-group analogue.
object.source_name: Asieh Sattari, Majid Arezoomand and Mohammad A. Iranmanesh, “On -groups and -groups”, arXiv:2003.06624 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.06624

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2020).

object.title: Alon–Tarsi bound for vertex-face graphs of plane graphs
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a plane graph, and let $G_{vf}$ denote its vertex-face graph. The **Alon–Tarsi conjecture.** Every plane graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\operatorname{AT}(G_{vf})\leqslant 7.
$$

This would extend the corresponding list-colouring bound, whose optimality is unknown; the authors explain that proving non-vanishing of the relevant graph-polynomial monomial would establish the claim.
object.source_name: Jarosław Grytczuk, Stanislav Jendrol' and Mariusz Zając, “Graph polynomials and paintability of plane graphs”, arXiv:2004.02159 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.02159

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2020).

object.title: The cactus-graph probability conjecture for sparse random graphs
object.statement: Let $A(n,m)$ denote the random graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. For $1/2<\alpha<1$, set $m=\alpha n$. **Cactus-graph probability conjecture.** The probability that $A(n,m)$ is a cactus graph is bounded away from $0$ and $1$. This conjecture asks how the probability of being a cactus graph behaves in the linear-edge regime; the supplied text gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
object.source_name: Mihyun Kang and Michael Missethan, “The giant component and 2-core in sparse random outerplanar graphs”, arXiv:2004.13319 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.13319

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2020).

object.title: Algebraic freeness conjecture for molecules with spherical boundary
object.statement: Let $\mathcal{S}$ be the class of molecules with spherical boundary. **Algebraic freeness conjecture.** The class $\mathcal{S}$ of molecules with spherical boundary is algebraically free. This extends the known algebraic freeness of totally loop-free molecules to the class of molecules with spherical boundary; the source provides no resolution of the conjecture.
object.source_name: Amar Hadzihasanovic, “Diagrammatic sets and rewriting in weak higher categories”, arXiv:2007.14505 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.14505

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2020).

object.title: Aboulker et al.'s cycle-orientation conjecture
object.statement:
Let $C$ be an undirected cycle, and orient each edge of $C$ to obtain a digraph.

**Aboulker et al.'s cycle-orientation conjecture.** Every orientation of a cycle is $\delta^+$-maderian.

The paper proves this statement, so this proposed special case of Mader's conjecture is resolved.
object.source_name: Lior Gishboliner, Raphael Steiner and Tibor Szabó, “Oriented cycles in digraphs of large outdegree”, arXiv:2008.13224 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.13224

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2020).

object.title: Out-leaf extension conjecture for maderian digraphs
object.statement:
Let $F$ be a $\delta^+$-maderian digraph and let $v_0\in V(F)$. Form $F^\ast$ by adding a new vertex $v_1$ and the arc $(v_0,v_1)$.

**Out-leaf extension conjecture.** The digraph $F^\ast$ is $\delta^+$-maderian as well.

This is described as an important step toward the forest-orientation conjecture and remains open in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Lior Gishboliner, Raphael Steiner and Tibor Szabó, “Oriented cycles in digraphs of large outdegree”, arXiv:2008.13224 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.13224

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2020).

object.title: Ergodicity of the aperiodic Ehrenfest wind-tree gas
object.statement: Consider an aperiodic Ehrenfest wind-tree gas whose scatterer configuration satisfies the conditions of the wind-tree flow cited in the source. **Ergodicity conjecture.** The aperiodic Ehrenfest wind-tree gas is ergodic. This is one of two proposed ergodicity conjectures for wind-tree gases, intended to illustrate ergodicity without local hyperbolicity; the supplied context gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Péter Bálint, Thomas Gilbert, Domokos Szász and Imre Péter Tóth, “What mathematical billiards teach us about statistical physics?”, arXiv:2009.06284 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.06284

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2020).

object.title: Conjecture that the balanced matching parameter equals two
object.statement:
Let $\textsc{bm}(n,n,\ldots,n)$ denote the balanced matching parameter with $n$ entries, each equal to $n$. **Balanced matching conjecture.**

$$
\textsc{bm}(\underbrace{n,n,\ldots,n}_{\text{$n$ times}})=2.
$$

The source says that a theorem gives the lower bound $\textsc{bm}(n,n,\ldots,n)\geq2$ and conjectures that this lower bound is sharp; no resolution is supplied.
object.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Eli Berger, Joseph Briggs, Erel Segal-Halevi and Shira Zerbib, “Fractionally balanced hypergraphs and rainbow KKM theorems”, arXiv:2011.01053 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.01053

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2020).

object.title: The middle-weight conjecture for binary projective three-weight codes
object.statement:
Let $C$ be a projective binary $[n,k]_2$ three-weight code with non-zero weights $w_1<w_2<w_3$.

**Middle-weight conjecture.** If

$$
w_1+w_2+w_3=\frac{3n}{2},
$$

then

$$
w_2=\frac{n}{2}.
$$

The conjecture is prompted by the feasible cases listed in the paper. It is the binary case of the proposed $q$-ary statement below and is presented as an open conjecture.
object.source_name: Michael Kiermaier, Sascha Kurz, Patrick Solé, Michael Stoll and Alfred Wassermann, “On strongly walk regular graphs, triple sum sets and their codes”, arXiv:2012.06160 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.06160

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2020). “So, it is an interesting open question, if $3$-SWRGs obtained from the coset graph of the dual code of a projective three-weight code also have to satisfy this extra condition.”

object.title: Hamming graph distinct-eigenvalue conjecture
object.statement:
Let $H(d,q)$ be the Hamming scheme on $Q^d$, where $Q$ is a set of size $q$, and let $H(d,q,j)$ be its distance-$j$ graph.

**Hamming distinct-eigenvalue conjecture.** If $H(d,q,j)$ is connected, it has more than $d/2$ distinct eigenvalues.

The paper explicitly states that this conjecture remains open.
object.source_name: Sebastian M. Cioabă and Himanshu Gupta, “On the eigenvalues of Grassmann graphs, Bilinear forms graphs and Hermitian forms graphs”, arXiv:2102.10155 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.10155

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2021). “The following conjecture was also posed in (see Conjecture 2.11) and is still open.”

object.title: The substitution-closure lwqo conjecture for permutation classes
object.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a permutation class, and let $\langle\mathcal{C}\rangle$ denote its substitution closure. **The substitution-closure conjecture.** If $\langle\mathcal{C}\rangle$ is wqo, then $\mathcal{C}$, and hence also $\langle\mathcal{C}\rangle$, is lwqo. This is the substitution-closure analogue of the conjecture for one-point extensions and remains open.
object.source_name: Robert Brignall and Vincent Vatter, “Labelled well-quasi-order for permutation classes”, arXiv:2103.08243 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.08243

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2021).

object.title: Huczynska–Vatter conjecture on finite bases of monotone grid classes
object.statement: A **monotone grid class** is a permutation class defined by a finite grid whose nonempty cells contain monotone permutations. **Huczynska–Vatter's conjecture.** Every monotone grid class is finitely based. The conjecture concerns monotone grid classes rather than directly addressing lwqo; the source notes that, unlike the geometric case, no nonconstructive proof was known there.
object.source_name: Robert Brignall and Vincent Vatter, “Labelled well-quasi-order for permutation classes”, arXiv:2103.08243 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.08243

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2021).

object.title: The core conjecture for right-angled Artin groups
object.statement:
Let $G=\Gamma(\Gamma,\{\mathbb Z\})$ and $G'=\Gamma(\Gamma',\{\mathbb Z\})$ be right-angled Artin groups. **Core conjecture.** Then

$$
G\equiv G'
$$

if and only if the cores of $G$ and $G'$ are isomorphic. This proposes that the core is a complete invariant of the elementary theory of a right-angled Artin group.
object.source_name: Montserrat Casals-Ruiz, Ilya Kazachkov and Javier de la Nuez González, “On the elementary theory of graph products of groups”, arXiv:2106.03782 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.03782

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2021). “This is indeed the case as proven by Sela and Kharlampovich-Miasnikov.”

object.title: Constant-length enumeration conjecture for fully commutative elements in $G(m,m,3)$
object.statement: Consider the complex reflection group $G(m,m,3)$ with its affine generating set, and let $\ell$ denote the length of an element. **Constant-length enumeration conjecture.** When $\ell>1$, the number of fully commutative elements of length $\ell$ is $6$. This is a pattern observed in the enumerative data for $G(m,m,3)$; no proof or resolution is given in the supplied source.
object.source_name: Jiayuan Wang, “A note on fully commutative elements in complex reflection groups”, arXiv:2109.09773 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.09773

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2021).

object.title: The disjoint-edge lower bound for dense geometric graphs
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a geometric graph with $2|E(G)|\geq |V(G)|$. **The disjoint-edge lower-bound conjecture.** Then

$$
|DJ(G)|\geq \frac{n}{2}\cdot \binom{d(G)}{3}.
$$

This conjecture gives a lower bound for the number of disjoint edge pairs in a sufficiently edge-dense geometric graph. The source gives no resolution, so the claim remains open.
object.source_name: Nikita Chernega, Alexandr Polyanskii and Rinat Sadykov, “Disjoint edges in geometric graphs”, arXiv:2111.05425 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.05425

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2021).
